question: An electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum has electric field amplitude $E_0 = 150\text{ V m}^{-1}$. Calculate the amplitude of the magnetic field. Also explain the relation between electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave.

options.A:
$B_0=\dfrac{c}{E_0}=2.0\times10^6\text{ T}$.
The electric and magnetic fields are parallel to each other and to the direction of propagation.
options.B:
$B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}=5.0\times10^{-5}\text{ T}$.
The fields have different frequencies and are out of phase.
options.C:
$B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}=\dfrac{150}{3.0\times10^8}=5.0\times10^{-7}\text{ T}$.
$\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are mutually perpendicular, both are perpendicular to propagation, and they are in phase with the same frequency.
options.D:
$B_0=E_0c=4.5\times10^{10}\text{ T}$.
The magnetic field is parallel to the propagation direction and the electric field is perpendicular to it.
